title: Signature Yearkeeper: The Anniversary Clock of the House
body:
Specifications. The Signature Yearkeeper is an original Signature design for a household anniversary clock, standing 28 centimetres tall under a glass dome, with a four-ball torsion pendulum and a brass movement wound once a year on the household's chosen date. Its dial is cream with black Roman numerals, and its base is walnut. This is a Signature-original design, never an authentic historic record.

Mechanism. A torsion spring matched to the four-ball pendulum gives a rotation cycle of about fifteen seconds, and the mainspring barrel delivers power for over 400 days. The escapement gives the pendulum one small impulse per cycle, and the train converts the slow rotation into the hands' motion. The clock is wound through the base with a single key.

Maintenance. Wind once a year on the household date, keep the dome on, dust the dome weekly, and service the movement every seven years. Lock the pendulum before moving the clock, and level it after every move.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the walnut base with a felt seal for the dome, fit the suspension spring by its blocks only, and regulate the clock in its final spot over a fortnight before delivery.

Tools. Winding key, dome cloth, spirit level, service log.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Yearkeeper torsion pendulum case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Solstice Clock: The Four-Season Torsion Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Solstice Clock is an original Signature design whose dial marks the solstices and equinoxes alongside the months, standing 30 centimetres tall with a disc-and-ball pendulum that rotates once per cycle under a tall dome. Its movement is a 400-day torsion movement, and its base carries a small season ring that the owner turns at each solstice. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The torsion pendulum regulates the going train as in any anniversary clock, and the season ring is a hand-set calendar aid, not a driven complication: the owner moves it at the solstice or equinox, and it simply records the season. Keeping the calendar hand-set avoids the extra gearing that would drain the mainspring's long power reserve.

Maintenance. Wind annually, turn the season ring at each solstice and equinox, keep the dome on, and service every seven years. Do not force the season ring past its stops.

Build and restoration guidance. Fit the season ring with clear stops and labels, balance the disc-and-ball pendulum before fitting, and prove the clock runs a full fortnight in beat before delivery.

Tools. Season ring chart, dome cloth, winding key, level.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Solstice pendulum case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Moonrise Clock: The Lunar Anniversary Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Moonrise Clock is an original Signature design that pairs a 400-day torsion movement with a hand-set moon-phase disc on the dial, standing 27 centimetres tall under a dome. The moon disc is set by hand from an almanac and shows the moon's age at a glance, while the torsion pendulum keeps the time. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The going train and torsion pendulum keep time exactly as in a standard anniversary clock. The moon disc is independent: it is turned by hand to the correct phase and then stays fixed, serving as a reference rather than a driven indication. This separation keeps the power reserve intact, since no extra gearing drains the mainspring.

Maintenance. Wind annually, set the moon disc monthly from an almanac, keep the dome on, and service every seven years. Handle the moon disc by its edge, never by its painted face.

Build and restoration guidance. Paint the moon disc with durable enamel, fit it with a smooth hand-setting action, and balance the pendulum before fitting the dial, so the dial work never disturbs the beat.

Tools. Almanac, moon-disc chart, winding key, dome cloth.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Moonrise pendulum case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Heirloom Clock: The Engraved Presentation Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Heirloom Clock is an original Signature design for presentation and inheritance, standing 29 centimetres tall with an engraved brass base plate for names and dates, a four-ball pendulum, and a glass dome. Its movement is a 400-day torsion movement, and the engraving is done before assembly so the plate is never engraved over a fitted movement. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The movement follows the standard anniversary pattern: mainspring barrel, going train, escapement and torsion pendulum with a matched suspension spring. The engraved base is purely commemorative and carries no mechanical function, so it never affects the rate or the power reserve.

Maintenance. Wind annually on the presentation date, polish the brass base gently without abrasive compounds, keep the dome on, and service every seven years. Record the presentation date and the winding date together in the base.

Build and restoration guidance. Engrave the base plate before fitting the movement, protect the engraving during assembly, and deliver the clock with a written winding-date card for the recipient.

Tools. Engraving tools, winding-date card, dome cloth, level.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Heirloom annual winding case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Garden Room Clock: The Conservatory Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Garden Room Clock is an original Signature design for a conservatory or garden room, standing 26 centimetres tall with a moisture-resistant base, a four-ball pendulum, and a dome sealed against humidity. Its movement is a 400-day torsion movement with a rust-resistant suspension spring. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The torsion pendulum and train work as in any anniversary clock, but the suspension spring is specified in a corrosion-resistant steel and the base seal is tighter, so humid air does not condense on the movement. The dome still lifts straight up for winding and service.

Maintenance. Keep the clock out of direct sun even in a garden room, wipe condensation from the dome promptly, wind annually, and inspect the suspension spring yearly for any sign of corrosion. Service every five years rather than seven in a humid room.

Build and restoration guidance. Fit the moisture-resistant base seal before the movement, prove the dome seal with a humidity test, and regulate the clock in the garden room itself, not in a dry workshop.

Tools. Humidity meter, dome cloth, corrosion-resistant spring stock, winding key.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Garden Room pendulum, stiffer spring case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Scholar's Clock: The Study Anniversary Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Scholar's Clock is an original Signature design for a study, standing 25 centimetres tall with a dark bronze base, a disc pendulum engraved with a compass rose, and a quiet 400-day movement. Its dial is plain and highly legible, with no decoration that distracts from reading the time. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The disc pendulum's inertia is matched to its suspension spring for a fifteen-second rotation cycle, and the going train is standard anniversary pattern. The disc's engraved compass rose is decoration only and is balanced so it does not disturb the rotation.

Maintenance. Wind annually, dust the dome weekly, keep the clock away from the study radiator, and service every seven years. Check the disc for wobble at each winding, since a bent disc is the commonest fault in a disc-pendulum clock.

Build and restoration guidance. Balance the engraved disc on a knife edge before fitting, fit the suspension spring by its blocks, and prove the rotation is clean and even over a full day before delivery.

Tools. Disc balancer, dome cloth, winding key, level.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Scholar's disc pendulum case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Wedding Clock: The Pair of Anniversary Clocks
body:
Specifications. The Signature Wedding Clock is an original Signature design sold as a matched pair: two 400-day anniversary clocks, one with a four-ball pendulum and one with a disc pendulum, both standing 27 centimetres tall, both wound on the wedding anniversary each year. Their bases are engraved as a pair, and their dials match exactly. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. Each clock is an independent 400-day torsion movement, and the pair is matched only in appearance and winding date, not mechanically linked. Matching the dials and the rates is a matter of regulating both clocks in the same room over the same fortnight, so they keep step as a pair.

Maintenance. Wind both clocks on the anniversary, service both together every seven years, and keep both domes on. If one clock's rate drifts from the other's, regulate the drifting clock alone, never by adjusting the good one to match it.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the pair from one dial drawing, regulate both in the same room, and deliver them with a single winding-date card covering both clocks.

Tools. Pair winding card, dome cloths, winding keys, rate log.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Wedding pair torsion cycle case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Traveller's Clock: The Cased Anniversary Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Traveller's Clock is an original Signature design for owners who move house often: a 400-day anniversary clock in a fitted travelling case, with a pendulum lock, a separate dome box, and a base that carries its own spirit level. It stands 24 centimetres tall out of its case. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The movement is standard anniversary pattern, and the travelling case adds only protection: a pendulum lock that holds the torsion mass still, a dome box that prevents glass breakage, and a level in the base so the clock can be set up correctly in a new home without a separate tool.

Maintenance. Lock the pendulum before every move, pack the dome separately, level the clock in its new spot, and observe the rotation for a day before judging the rate. Wind annually on a fixed date regardless of moves.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the case to fit the clock exactly, with cut-outs for the pendulum lock and the winding key, and fix a release checklist inside the case lid.

Tools. Travelling case, pendulum lock, dome box, base level.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Traveller's annual winding case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Library Clock: The Silent Anniversary Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Library Clock is an original Signature design for a library, standing 26 centimetres tall with a four-ball pendulum, a 400-day movement, and no strike or chime of any kind, so it is silent in use. Its dial is large and plain for reading across a reading room. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The going train and torsion pendulum keep time silently, and the absence of any strike train means the full mainspring power goes to timekeeping, which helps the clock reach its full 400-day reserve. The rotating balls are the only moving display, and they turn too slowly to make any sound.

Maintenance. Wind annually, dust the dome weekly, keep the clock out of draughts from library doors, and service every seven years. A library clock that stops is almost always dusty or draughted, not broken.

Build and restoration guidance. Fit the movement with no strike work at all, rather than a silenced strike, so there is nothing to rattle or wear. Regulate the clock in the library itself over a fortnight.

Tools. Dome cloth, winding key, level, service log.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Library pendulum case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Winter Clock: The Cold-Room Anniversary Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Winter Clock is an original Signature design for a cold room, standing 27 centimetres tall with a temperature-stable suspension spring, a four-ball pendulum, and a dome seal that resists condensation. Its movement is a 400-day torsion movement specified for rooms that fall near freezing in winter. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The suspension spring is chosen for low temperature sensitivity, so the rotation period changes less with the seasons than a standard spring would. The train oil is cold-rated, and the dome seal keeps damp air off the movement during freeze and thaw cycles.

Maintenance. Inspect the suspension spring each autumn, wipe condensation promptly, wind annually, and use cold-rated oil at every service. Log the rate with the room temperature through the winter.

Build and restoration guidance. Fit the cold-rated spring and oil before delivery, prove the dome seal with a cold test, and regulate the clock in a cold room, not a warm workshop.

Tools. Cold-rated oil, temperature log, dome cloth, winding key.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Winter pendulum, cold room case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Observatory Clock: The Star-Dial Anniversary Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Observatory Clock is an original Signature design for an observatory study, standing 30 centimetres tall with a dial that shows the time alongside a hand-set star chart ring, a four-ball pendulum, and a 400-day movement. The star ring is set by hand from an almanac, like the moon disc of the Moonrise design. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The torsion pendulum and going train keep time, and the star ring is a hand-set reference that does not drain the mainspring. The owner turns the ring to the current sky at the start of an observing session and reads the time and the sky together.

Maintenance. Wind annually, set the star ring at each observing session, keep the dome on, and service every seven years. Handle the star ring by its edge to protect its markings.

Build and restoration guidance. Print the star ring on durable stock, fit it with a smooth hand-setting action, and balance the pendulum before fitting the dial.

Tools. Almanac, star-ring chart, winding key, dome cloth.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Observatory train stage case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Museum Clock: The Working Exhibit Anniversary Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Museum Clock is an original Signature design for a museum case, standing 28 centimetres tall with a glass-fronted display base that lets visitors see the torsion pendulum from below as well as through the dome, a four-ball pendulum, and a 400-day movement. Its base carries a label explaining the torsion principle in plain language. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The movement is standard anniversary pattern, and the display base adds a mirror or a glass panel so the rotating pendulum can be watched from underneath without opening the case. The label explains that the pendulum rotates rather than swings, and that one winding lasts about 400 days.

Maintenance. Clean the dome and the display panel weekly, wind annually, service every seven years, and check the label's fixings at each winding. Keep the case lighting cool so heat does not affect the spring.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the display base with a locked service panel, fit cool lighting, and prove the pendulum can be seen clearly from the visitor's side before installation.

Tools. Display cloth, cool-light meter, winding key, label kit.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Museum torsion cycle case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Jubilee Clock: The Fifty-Year Anniversary Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Jubilee Clock is an original Signature design for a fiftieth anniversary, standing 32 centimetres tall, the tallest in this Signature set, with a six-ball pendulum, a gilt base, and a 400-day movement. Its dial is cream with gold numerals, and its base carries a jubilee inscription plate. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The six-ball pendulum has a larger moment of inertia than a four-ball pendulum, so it is paired with a stiffer suspension spring to keep the rotation cycle near fifteen seconds. The going train is standard anniversary pattern, and the larger pendulum is balanced so all six balls contribute equally to the rotation.

Maintenance. Wind annually on the jubilee date, polish the gilt base gently, keep the dome on, and service every seven years. Check all six balls for tightness at each winding, since a loose ball unbalances the rotation.

Build and restoration guidance. Balance the six-ball pendulum as a set before fitting, match the spring stiffness to the six-ball inertia, and regulate over a fortnight in the final spot.

Tools. Six-ball balance gauge, gilt polish cloth, winding key, level.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Jubilee six-ball pendulum case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Night Clock: The Low-Light Anniversary Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Night Clock is an original Signature design for a bedroom, standing 25 centimetres tall with luminous dial markings, a four-ball pendulum, and a 400-day movement that is silent in use. Its dome is lightly tinted to soften the luminous dial at night without hiding the rotating balls. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The movement is standard silent anniversary pattern, and the luminous markings are charged by daylight and glow at night without any battery or lamp. The tinted dome reduces glare while still showing the pendulum's slow rotation, which is the clock's main night-time display.

Maintenance. Wind annually, keep the clock where daylight reaches the dial so the markings charge, dust the dome weekly, and service every seven years. Replace luminous markings only with modern safe materials, never with historic luminous compounds.

Build and restoration guidance. Fit the luminous markings before the dial is fitted, prove they charge in daylight and glow at night, and test the tinted dome for clarity in both day and night light.

Tools. Daylight test card, dome cloth, winding key, level.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Night Clock annual winding case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Archive Clock: The Record-Keeper's Anniversary Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Archive Clock is an original Signature design for an archive or record office, standing 27 centimetres tall with a four-ball pendulum, a 400-day movement, and a base drawer that holds a winding and service logbook. Its dial is plain and highly legible, and its base is oak. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The movement is standard anniversary pattern, and the base drawer adds only record-keeping: the logbook records every winding date, every service, every suspension change and every regulation, so the clock's full history travels with the clock. The drawer is fitted so it cannot be opened without lifting the dome, which prevents the logbook being lost separately.

Maintenance. Wind annually and write the date in the logbook at once, service every seven years and record the work, and keep the logbook in the drawer. A clock with a complete logbook is worth more and is easier to repair than one without.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the drawer to fit the logbook exactly, fit the dome so it must be lifted to open the drawer, and deliver the clock with the first winding date already entered.

Tools. Logbook, oak drawer gauge, winding key, dome cloth.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Archive dial case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Grand Anniversary Clock: The Exhibition Master Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Grand Anniversary Clock is an original Signature design for exhibition, standing 35 centimetres tall, the largest in this Signature set, with an eight-ball pendulum, a temperature-stable suspension spring, a moon-phase hand-set disc, a season ring, and a 400-day movement. Its base is walnut with a gilt inscription plate, and its dome is the tallest in the set. This is a Signature-original design, the most complex in this Signature set.

Mechanism. The eight-ball pendulum's large inertia is paired with a stiff suspension spring to hold the rotation cycle near fifteen seconds, and the going train is standard anniversary pattern with a mainspring barrel sized for the full 400-day reserve despite the heavier pendulum. The moon disc and season ring are hand-set references that drain no power, so the grand design keeps the long reserve of a simple anniversary clock while displaying more information.

Maintenance. Wind annually, set the moon disc monthly and the season ring at each solstice and equinox, check all eight balls for tightness at each winding, service every seven years, and keep the dome on at all times. Regulate only in the exhibition spot, over a full fortnight.

Build and restoration guidance. Balance the eight-ball pendulum as a set, match the spring to the eight-ball inertia, fit the moon disc and season ring with smooth hand-setting actions, and prove the clock runs a full month in beat before exhibition.

Tools. Eight-ball balance gauge, moon-disc chart, season-ring chart, winding key.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Grand eight-ball pendulum case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.
